definitions.explanation: One of the five major styles of Chinese/Japanese calligraphy. A flowing style between the rigid block script and the highly abbreviated cursive script, commonly used in everyday handwriting.

examples.japanese: {行書|ぎょうしょ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{名前|なまえ}→名前：02234_namae⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{書|か}く→書く：00477_kaku⟧。
examples.english: To write one's name in semi-cursive script.

examples.japanese: {行書|ぎょうしょ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{楷書|かいしょ}→楷書：13247_kaisho⟧⟦より→より：09476_yori⟧⟦{速|はや}く→速い：00514_hayai⟧⟦{書|か}ける→書く：00477_kaku⟧。
examples.english: Semi-cursive script can be written faster than block script.

examples.japanese: ⟦{書道|しょどう}→書道：04178_shodou⟧⟦{教室|きょうしつ}→教室：00794_kyoushitsu⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{楷書|かいしょ}→楷書：13247_kaisho⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{次|つぎ}→次：00819_tsugi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{行書|ぎょうしょ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{習|なら}った→習う：00479_narau⟧。
examples.english: In calligraphy class, I learned semi-cursive script after block script.

notes: Composed of ⟦{行|ぎょう}→行：26669_gyou⟧ (go, move, flow) + ⟦{書|しょ}→〜書：28467_sho⟧ (writing, script). One of the five traditional script styles ({五体|ごたい}): {篆書|てんしょ} (seal script), {隷書|れいしょ} (clerical script), ⟦{楷書|かいしょ}→楷書：13247_kaisho⟧ (block/regular script), {行書|ぎょうしょ} (semi-cursive), and ⟦{草書|そうしょ}→草書：19196_sousho⟧ (cursive). {行書|ぎょうしょ} is considered the most practical for everyday use — it simplifies strokes of ⟦{楷書|かいしょ}→楷書：13247_kaisho⟧ while remaining readable, unlike the highly abbreviated ⟦{草書|そうしょ}→草書：19196_sousho⟧. Japanese handwriting naturally tends toward {行書|ぎょうしょ} when writing quickly.
